solution: Krishna III is also known as 'Tanjaikonda' (conqueror of Thanjavur). He took the Rashtrakuta empire to new heights in the south.

question: Whose court poet was Bharavi, the author of the epic 'Kiratarjuniyam'?
solution: Kiratarjuniyam describes the battle between Arjuna and Shiva in the form of Kirat. It is considered one of the most difficult poems in Sanskrit literature.

question: Who wrote the first poetic book of Kannada language 'Kavirajamarg'?
solution: Amoghavarsha himself was a great writer. His reign is considered to be the golden age of Kannada language and culture.

question: What is the essence of 'Vesara style' of Chalukya temple architecture?
options: Mixture of Nagara and Dravidian styles
solution: Fine examples of Vesara style are found in the temples of Badami, Aihole and Pattadakal. Pattadakal is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

question: Who is the author of 'Nitisar', which is called the Arthashastra of the Gupta period?
solution: Nitisara describes the duties of the king, war strategies and diplomacy. It is the main source of political thought of the Gupta period.

question: What were the silver coins issued by the Gupta emperors called?
solution: The rupaka weighed about 32 grains and was based on imitations of Shaka coins.

question: What was the main function of 'Sandhivigrahik' officer?
solution: Harishen was also posted on the post of Sandhivigrahika during the time of Samudragupta. This post was very important for diplomacy.

question: Who defeated Harshavardhana on the banks of river Narmada?
solution: This war was an important turning point in Indian history. This information is available from the Aihole inscription and the accounts of Hiuen Tsang.

question: Raja Bhoj was the most famous ruler of which dynasty?
solution: Raja Bhoj wrote many important texts like 'Saraswatikanthabharan' and 'Samarangan Sutradhar'. The city of Bhopal is named after him.

question: Rashtrakuta king Amoghavarsha I was a follower of which religion?
solution: Amoghavarsha is called 'Ashoka of the South' because he gave importance to peace and literature instead of war. He had written a book named 'Ratnamalika'.

question: Where was the capital of Hoysala dynasty?
solution: Hoysala kings built 'stellate' shaped temples. The carvings of his temples are famous throughout the world.

question: Which special title did Samudragupta hold?
solution: Samudragupta's other titles also include Param Bhagavata, Licchavi Dauhitra and Apratiratha. Lichchavi Dauhitra means son of a Lichchavi princess.

question: Where did Rashtrakuta king Amoghavarsha shift his capital?
solution: Manyakhet remained the main center of Rashtrakuta power till the end and was famous for its prosperity.

question: Where did Rashtrakuta king Krishna III build a victory pillar and temple to commemorate his victories?
solution: Krishna III was one of the greatest warriors of the Rashtrakuta dynasty who completely suppressed the Chola power for some time.

question: Who was the last king of the 'Badami' branch of the Chalukya dynasty?
solution: Kirtivarman II proved to be a weak ruler, paving the way for the rise of the Rashtrakutas in the Deccan.

question: The inscription in which language describes the achievements of Chalukya king Pulakeshin II?
solution: In this inscription, Ravi Kirti has compared Pulakeshin II to the gods and praised his military power.

question: Which religion was given special protection by 'Harshavardhana' after the Gupta period?
solution: In Kannauj, Harsha organized a huge religious gathering to propagate the Mahayana school of Buddhism.

question: Chandragupta I strengthened his political position by marrying which princess?
solution: The matrimonial alliance with the Licchavis helped transform the Guptas from a regional power into an empire. Chandragupta I had also inscribed the name of Kumaradevi on his coins.

question: Which three famous plays were written by Harshavardhan?
solution: The influence of Buddhism is visible in Harsha's plays, especially in Nagananda. He was also a patron of scholars.

question: What was the head of a district (subject) called in the Gupta period?
solution: To assist the Vishyapati, there was a council which included the main traders and artists of the city.

question: In which area was the role of 'Nagar Shresthi' and 'Sarthavaha' maximum in the Gupta period?
options: In urban and business administration, they were the main members of the city council who decided economic and civic policies.
Gramika was prominent here in rural development.
Here priests and Acharyas were prominent in religious rituals.
In military campaigns, the army was led by Mahabaladhikrit.
solution: This shows that the middle class and traders had a good participation in governance during the Gupta period.

question: According to the play 'Devi Chandraguptam', to protect whom did Chandragupta II kill the Shaka king?
solution: This play of Visakhadutta throws light on a dark chapter of the Gupta dynasty, which is also confirmed by other later literary evidence.

question: How did Chandragupta II attain power?
options: Got power directly by defeating foreign invaders
solution: Chandragupta II not only murdered his brother but also married his widow Dhruvadevi so that the dignity and security of the kingdom was maintained.

question: Which city became the center of politics in North India after the Gupta period?
solution: Pala, Pratihara and Rashtrakuta kings fought long wars for Kannauj. It was also called 'Mahodaya Nagar'.

question: How did Chalukya king Pulakeshin II meet his end?
options: He was killed in battle at the hands of Narasimhavarman I. He attained martyrdom while defending his capital during the Pallava invasion in 642 AD.
solution: After the death of Pulakeshin II the Chalukya Empire remained under the control of the Pallavas for about 13 years, until Vikramaditya I won it back.

question: In which book did 'Varahamihir' tell that the Earth is round and it pulls objects towards itself due to gravity?
solution: Varahamihir provided scientific basis to ancient Indian science. He had accurately calculated the movements of the planets.

question: Which title did Chandragupta II take after his victory over the Shakas?
solution: Chandragupta II is also called Shakari (enemy of the Shakas). He issued special silver coins to commemorate this victory.

question: According to Fa Hien, what did people use for exchange during the Gupta period?
options: Cowries were in circulation only with grain
solution: The use of cowries shows that the availability of small currency for the general public was limited or that they carried out simple trade.

question: Why is the Eran Inscription (510 AD) important?
options: Kumargupta's inscriptions are important for the establishment of Nalanda.
The first written evidence of the practice of Sati
Prayag Prashasti is famous for the victories of Samudragupta.
Bhitari inscription is famous for the defeat of Huns.
solution: Eran inscription located in Sagar district of Madhya Pradesh is very famous as the historical evidence of the practice of Sati in Indian society.

question: Who took the title of 'Ashwamedha Parakramaank'?
solution: Samudragupta also issued Ashwamedha type gold coins, which had a sacrificial horse on one side and the picture of Queen Dattadevi on the other.

question: Who was the founder of Gupta dynasty?
solution: The Gupta dynasty was founded by Shri Gupta. In history he has been given the title of Maharaj. After him his son Ghatotkacha became the ruler. The Gupta period is called the golden age of Indian history.

question: The picture of which bird is found in place of Garuda on the coins of Samudragupta?
solution: Garuda was the state symbol of the Guptas. The depiction of the king on coins reflected his religious faith and conquests.

question: Ellora caves contain caves related to which religion?
solution: Ellora caves are a symbol of Indian religious tolerance. The Rashtrakutas provided protection to all these religions.
